kpis.label: $10B EXIM loan + ~$2B private capital; demand-driven stockpile spanning the USGS's full 60-mineral critical list, tied to OEM offtake commitments (GM and others)

Stock's best week since September as the Q2 print (adjusted EBITDA positive for the first time) was followed by Project Swarm (launched Jul 30, pre-selling 10X magnet output to drone/motor makers) and a new 9-figure gadolinium deal with an unnamed US aerospace/defense customer, disclosed Aug 13

Fresh all-time high as Washington's copper-tariff decision — due from Commerce Secretary Lutnick by Jun 30 — remains overdue by more than a month; 2026 YTD gain now ~18.6%, keeping Freeport's leverage to the metal in focus

Vote set for Aug 28 is management's 'final remaining closing condition' with no regulatory hurdles left — even as USAR's own Q2 revenue missed badly ($5.82M vs. $8.05M est.), knocking shares ~9% after hours

themes.title: Beijing weaponizing processing dominance
themes.description: Ex-China rare-earth prices remain far above pre-controls levels after Beijing's April-2025 move — European dysprosium still around $2,250/kg (~8x), terbium ~5x, yttrium oxide up to ~140x to ~$1,100/kg — and shipments of yttrium, dysprosium and terbium into the US remain down roughly 50% versus pre-control levels. A May 2026 Trump-Xi summit in Beijing raised hopes of extending the truce, but analysts describe the pause as functionally over already.

themes.title: Truce getting tested
themes.description: China's Jun 22 entity-list additions targeted MP Materials and USA Rare Earth — the two largest recipients of US federal rare-earth investment, at $550M and $1.6B respectively — and remain unresolved heading into the Nov 10, 2026 truce deadline. Coverage increasingly frames multinationals as unprepared for a deeper crisis should Washington and Beijing fail to renegotiate the reprieve.

themes.title: Washington's playbook, compounding company by company
themes.description: Project Vault's $10B EXIM loan + ~$2B private capital remains the umbrella policy; on top of it, Energy Fuels' ASM acquisition won 98%+ shareholder approval Aug 12 (implementation Aug 28), MP Materials' Project Swarm is pre-selling 10X magnet capacity to drone and motor makers, and USA Rare Earth's Serra Verde vote (Aug 28) is now down to its last closing condition.

tiers.label: Established Producers
tiers.note: Tiered by maturity/risk — not a ranked buy list.

rows.angle: Only US rare-earth mine + processing (Mountain Pass); $500M Apple magnet offtake (shipments from 2027) + $400M DoD convertible preferred (DoD now largest shareholder, ~15%)
rows.watch for: Q2 call (Aug 13) revealed Project Swarm — launched Jul 30 to aggregate drone/motor magnet demand ahead of the 10X plant — plus a new 9-figure gadolinium deal with an unnamed US aerospace/defense customer; stock rallied 23.5% for the week even though it remains down roughly 28% over the past year. 10X plant (2028) still carries DoD's ≥$140M EBITDA guarantee at a $110/kg NdPr price floor; capex guidance reaffirmed at $500–600M

rows.angle: Largest non-China rare-earth producer (Australia/Malaysia); pushing into magnet metals
rows.watch for: FY2026 results land Aug 26 under interim CEO Pol Le Roux — the first full-year report since the leadership change and the A$750M equity raise announced last week; shares choppy into the print (+5.9% over 7 days, -7.4% over 90) as the market weighs Towards-2030 dilution against the JS Link Malaysia magnet partnership

Lithium is showing its first concrete signs of turning — China carbonate spot climbed to ¥148,000/t on Aug 12 off a 6-month low, and CRU models Q3 averaging $33,900/t (+49% QoQ) — but Citi cut its ALB price target to $175 from $225 on Aug 7, even after the Q2 beat (EPS $3.75 vs. $3.27 est., energy-storage realized pricing $19.53/kg vs. $12.17/kg a year ago). Zacks upgraded to a #2 (Buy) rank the same week — a genuinely mixed signal

rows.angle: Copper — the electrification metal at scale
rows.watch for: Copper hit a fresh Comex record of $6.77/lb intraday Aug 7 as Washington's tariff decision (due Jun 30) remains overdue by more than a month; 2026 YTD gain now ~18.6%. Grasberg Block Cave ramp on schedule and FY26 guidance reaffirmed, but at least one analysis now flags the stock as 'not an obvious bargain' after its multi-year run

tiers.label: Developers / Small-Cap — Speculative
tiers.note: Tiered by maturity/risk — not a ranked buy list.

rows.angle: US rare-earth mine-to-magnet aspirant; Texas mine + Oklahoma magnet plant; DoC $1.6B LOI + ~10% equity stake (Jan 2026, priced $17.17)
rows.watch for: Q2 revenue missed badly — $5.82M vs. $8.05M est., adjusted loss $0.15/share vs. $0.13 est. — and shares fell ~9% after hours; but the company closed its $1.6B DoC CHIPS funding in June and management called the Aug 28 Serra Verde vote the 'final remaining closing condition' with no regulatory hurdles left. Pela Ema (Brazil) is already in production; still on China's export-control entity list

rows.angle: Uranium + rare-earth processing at White Mesa
rows.watch for: ASM shareholders approved the acquisition Aug 12 with 98%+ in favor (implementation Aug 28), de-risking one of the two simultaneous deals toward a mine-to-magnet platform; the $1.9B VAC deal (magnet manufacturing) still needs to close. White Mesa uranium processing remains paused for maintenance until Q4 2026/early 2027; ~$1B liquidity

Aug 13 update: Thacker Pass hit 95% detailed engineering and 80%+ procurement, with $1.8B of the $2.93B capex budget spent as construction heads toward peak activity later this year; mechanical completion still targeted late 2027. The $175M Yorkville convertible-debenture facility from Aug 6 remains a relatively expensive financing structure layered on the $2.23B DoE loan

bear_case.title: Commodity cycles cut both ways
bear_case.description: Lithium is showing its first concrete signs of turning — China spot climbed to ¥148,000/t on Aug 12 off a 6-month low, and CRU's Q3 base case is $33,900/t, up ~49% QoQ — but Citi cut its Albemarle price target to $175 from $225 the same week even after an earnings beat. Copper is at record highs too, but one analysis already flags Freeport as 'not an obvious bargain' at today's levels. A price spike or a single strong quarter doesn't confirm a durable cycle turn.

bear_case.title: China can flood the market
bear_case.description: Beijing has both weaponized scarcity (yttrium oxide up ~140x since April 2025) and, historically, dumped supply when it suited its interests; analysts now describe the post-Busan pause as functionally over, with the Nov 10 truce deadline the key swing factor either way.

bear_case.title: Juniors dilute
bear_case.description: USA Rare Earth's Q2 revenue missed by 27% and shares fell ~9% after hours, yet the company is still issuing 126.85M new shares (34% of the combined company) to close Serra Verde; Lithium Americas has now spent $1.8B of Thacker Pass's $2.93B capex budget on top of the $175M Yorkville convertible facility layered onto its DoE loan. Building refining capacity remains expensive, and names without direct sovereign grants keep diluting to get there.

bear_case.title: Policy dependency
bear_case.description: Washington's own copper-tariff decision is now more than a month overdue past its Jun 30 deadline; Energy Fuels' $1.9B VAC deal still needs to close behind the newly-approved ASM acquisition; and the onshoring trade broadly leans on a truce Beijing has already tested once this quarter. A policy reversal or a durable détente both cut against the thesis, just in different ways.

positions.name: MP Materials
positions.note: Project Swarm and a new 9-figure gadolinium deal with an unnamed aerospace/defense customer (disclosed on the Aug 13 call) extend the demand-diversification story beyond Apple and DoD; stock rallied 23.5% for the week. Also appears in Robotics — hold it once, not twice.

positions.name: Freeport-McMoRan
positions.note: Copper hit a fresh Comex record ($6.77/lb, Aug 7) with Grasberg on schedule and FY26 guidance reaffirmed, but the stock is now being described as 'not an obvious bargain' after its run — a valuation flag worth watching even inside Core.

positions.name: Lynas Rare Earths
positions.note: FY2026 results (Aug 26) are the next real test of the Towards-2030 dilution thesis under a new interim CEO; no fresh evidence this week either way, so sizing is unchanged from the A$750M raise flagged last week.

positions.name: USA Rare Earth
positions.note: Q2 revenue missed by 27% and shares fell ~9% after hours — a real operating miss — even as management called the Aug 28 Serra Verde vote the final closing condition with no regulatory hurdles left; trimmed for the miss.

positions.name: Energy Fuels
positions.note: ASM shareholders approved the acquisition 98%+ on Aug 12, a genuine de-risking of one of the two simultaneous deals toward a mine-to-magnet platform; sized up to reflect it, though VAC and the conditional OSC loan remain open questions.

positions.name: Lithium Americas
positions.note: Thacker Pass hit 95% engineering and 80%+ procurement (Aug 13) — real construction progress — but it's funded partly by the expensive Yorkville convertible facility, so sizing is unchanged.

positions.name: Albemarle
positions.note: The clearest evidence yet that the lithium cycle may be turning — China spot at ¥148,000/t, CRU's Q3 forecast +49% QoQ — but Citi cut its own ALB price target to $175 from $225 the same week the stock beat, so the market hasn't confirmed the turn; stays a watch.
